short_definition: A security system monitoring and controlling incoming and outgoing network traffic based on rules.
layman_explanation: A bouncer standing at the network entrance checking IDs before letting data pass.

short_definition: An attack where the threat actor secretly intercepts and alters traffic between two parties.
layman_explanation: Someone secretly reading and altering paper letters passed between two people.

short_definition: Virtual Private Network encrypts an internet connection to protect identity and traffic.
layman_explanation: Driving your data through a private underground tunnel so outside observers can't see your activity.

short_definition: Overwhelming a target network or server with flooding traffic to cause service outage.
layman_explanation: Hiring a crowd of thousands of people to stand in a small store doorway so real customers can't enter.

short_definition: A device or software application that monitors a network for malicious activity or policy violations.
layman_explanation: A burglar alarm that sounds an alert when it detects a intruder inside the building.

short_definition: A network security tool that monitors traffic and actively blocks detected threats in real-time.
layman_explanation: An automated security system that detects an intruder and automatically locks security doors to block them.

short_definition: Altering the factory-assigned Media Access Control address of a network interface to impersonate another device.
layman_explanation: Changing your device's physical ID number so local Wi-Fi networks think you are an approved hardware device.

short_definition: Corrupting Domain Name System resolution tables to redirect web traffic to malicious IP addresses.
layman_explanation: Tampering with a phone directory so dialing your bank's number connects you to a scammer.

short_definition: Probing a server or host for open network ports to identify active services and vulnerabilities.
layman_explanation: A burglar walking down an apartment hallway checking every door handle to see which doors are unlocked.

short_definition: Intercepting and logging network traffic packets as they flow across a local network.
layman_explanation: Eavesdropping on a party phone line to listen to conversations passing by.

short_definition: An IT security solution that provides secure remote access to applications based on adaptive policies.
layman_explanation: Requiring continuous identity validation for every single room you enter, rather than trusting you once at the main gate.

short_definition: Dividing a computer network into smaller subnetworks to improve performance and security containment.
layman_explanation: Dividing a ship into watertight compartments so a leak in one area doesn't sink the entire vessel.

short_definition: Sending forged Address Resolution Protocol messages over a local network to link an attacker's MAC address with a legitimate IP.
layman_explanation: Shouting 'I am the post office!' on a local network so everyone sends their mail directly to you.

short_definition: A method of mapping an entire local network of private IP addresses to a single public IP address.
layman_explanation: An apartment building receptionist accepting all mail at one street address and distributing it internally.

short_definition: A perimeter subnetwork exposed to untrusted traffic, isolating internal networks from public services.
layman_explanation: A secure reception lobby sitting between the public street and the company's private back offices.

short_definition: A decoy computer system intended to attract cyberattacks and study attacker techniques.
layman_explanation: Setting up a fake bank vault with dummy money to trap burglars and study how they broke in.

short_definition: A DDoS attack exploiting TCP handshakes by sending incomplete connection requests to exhaust server resources.
layman_explanation: Calling a restaurant repeatedly, asking for a table, and hanging up before giving your name until all lines are jammed.

short_definition: Inspecting data packets against security criteria such as IP addresses, ports, and protocols before allowing entry.
layman_explanation: Inspecting outgoing and incoming envelopes for authorized return addresses before delivery.

short_definition: Firewall technology that tracks the operating state of active network connections to validate inbound traffic.
layman_explanation: A bouncer who remembers which guests went outside for fresh air so they can return without showing ID again.

short_definition: Advanced packet filtering that examines the actual data payload inside packets, not just protocol headers.
layman_explanation: Opening and reading every letter inside envelopes passing through the post office to check for contraband.

short_definition: A specially configured server designed to withstand attacks, serving as a single access portal for administrators.
layman_explanation: A reinforced security booth serving as the single entry point into a sensitive server room.

short_definition: An architecture that dynamically creates one-to-one network connections between users and specific resources.
layman_explanation: A dark building where individual office rooms only become visible when an approved worker unlocks them.

short_definition: A network physically isolated from all unsecured networks and the public internet.
layman_explanation: A secure computer sitting in a room with no internet cables, Wi-Fi chips, or external connections.

short_definition: A suite of protocols for securing Internet Protocol communications by authenticating and encrypting each IP packet.
layman_explanation: A set of rules for putting every piece of mail in an encrypted tamper-proof envelope before posting.

short_definition: A VPN configuration that routes some traffic through the secure VPN tunnel while other traffic accesses the public internet directly.
layman_explanation: Sending work emails through a secure armored truck while streaming music over normal public roads.

short_definition: An intermediary gateway server making requests on behalf of client devices to hide their origin.
layman_explanation: Asking a friend to buy something at a store for you so the cashier never sees who made the purchase.

short_definition: A server positioned in front of web servers to dispatch client requests, balance load, and provide security.
layman_explanation: A receptionist greeting all visitors and distributing them across available desks in a back office.

short_definition: An enterprise solution enforcing security policies on devices attempting to connect to a corporate network.
layman_explanation: Checking that a car has passed safety inspections before allowing it onto a private toll road.

short_definition: A distributed DoS attack that spoofs a target's IP address and pings broadcast addresses to flood the victim.
layman_explanation: Sending hundreds of mail letters with a victim's return address so everyone sends back mail to swamp them.

short_definition: A suite of specifications for securing information provided by the Domain Name System using cryptographic signatures.
layman_explanation: Adding an official wax seal to phone directories so callers know numbers haven't been tampered with.

short_definition: Creation of Internet Protocol packets with a forged source IP address to impersonate another computer.
layman_explanation: Writing someone else's return address on a letter to hide who actually sent it.

short_definition: Taking over an established TCP session between two connected machines by predicting sequence numbers.
layman_explanation: Jumping into an ongoing phone call after one person steps away and pretending to be them.

short_definition: Inferring sensitive information from patterns, frequency, and volume of network communications.
layman_explanation: Watching delivery trucks entering and leaving a factory to guess how much inventory is being produced.

short_definition: Intentional slowing of internet service speed by a network administrator or ISP.
layman_explanation: Limiting traffic flow on a highway to one lane during rush hour to manage congestion.

short_definition: An attack method sending packets to a port not normally accessible from a specific Virtual LAN.
layman_explanation: Sneaking through an unauthorized service corridor to access restricted floors in an office building.

short_definition: Falsely advertising ownership of IP address groups to reroute global internet traffic through rogue routers.
layman_explanation: Changing road signs on a major highway so all cross-country traffic passes through a fake toll booth.

short_definition: A DDoS technique where an attacker sends small requests with spoofed source IPs to generate massive response traffic against a target.
layman_explanation: Sending a tiny postcard asking 'Tell me your whole history' with a victim's return address so they get flooded with thick books.

short_definition: Directing external network traffic on a specific port to a specific internal device behind a router.
layman_explanation: Configuring a mailroom to send all mail labeled 'Department 80' straight to the web developer's desk.

short_definition: Monitoring and restricting outbound network traffic departing from a private internal network.
layman_explanation: Inspecting security guards checking backpacks at exit doors to ensure data isn't leaking out.

short_definition: Filtering incoming network traffic to ensure packets arrive from legitimate, expected IP ranges.
layman_explanation: Checking the return addresses on incoming letters to reject mail originating from known scam addresses.

short_definition: A networking protocol providing centralized Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting management for users.
layman_explanation: A central security desk verifying employee credentials before letting them connect to enterprise Wi-Fi.

short_definition: A remote authentication protocol offering separate authentication, authorization, and accounting services for network devices.
layman_explanation: A specialized access management system used specifically to control administrator logins to routers and switches.

short_definition: An attack forcing a web browser to communicate in plain text HTTP instead of encrypted HTTPS.
layman_explanation: Stealing an armored lockbox from a courier and replacing it with an unencrypted open paper bag.

short_definition: A hardware device installed directly on a network cable to copy passing traffic for monitoring without disruption.
layman_explanation: Attaching a physical wiretap onto a cable line to record data flow without slowing down connection speed.

short_definition: A network switch feature sending copies of network packets seen on one port to a monitoring port.
layman_explanation: Setting up a one-way mirror over a doorway so security teams can observe passing traffic without interference.

short_definition: A special IP address (127.0.0.1) used by a host to send network traffic back to itself for testing.
layman_explanation: Addressing a letter to yourself to test if your home mailbox is receiving mail properly.

short_definition: Routing malicious traffic away from intended targets by configuring DNS servers to return benign IP addresses.
layman_explanation: Diverting a flooded river into an empty field so it doesn't destroy a nearby town.

short_definition: Sending intentionally oversized network packets to crash network equipment unable to buffer them.
layman_explanation: Trying to stuff a giant wooden crate down a mail chute designed only for paper letters to jam the system.

short_definition: A network standard providing port-based Network Access Control for Ethernet and Wi-Fi networks.
layman_explanation: Requiring every device to present a digital security certificate before an Ethernet wall jack turns on.

short_definition: Compromising a network switch's MAC address table with fake entries to force it into hub mode.
layman_explanation: Stuffing a building's directory with thousands of fake names so receptionists give up and broadcast every visitor's name aloud.

short_definition: A network-level exploit targeting unpatched, undiscovered protocol vulnerabilities.
layman_explanation: Exploiting a newly discovered bug in router firmware before the hardware vendor releases an update.
